title: Ash Wallington, who greeted him at STVP — 'Incorruptible asks what comes next: once you discover genuine value, how do you build a company capable of protecting it?'
summary: A higher-education innovation lead who hosted Eric at Stanford's Technology Ventures Program frames the two books as a sequence: Lean Startup defined how a generation found value, and this one asks how to keep it. Her write-up reaches for Citizen Kane — Charles Foster Kane enthusiastically drafts a "Declaration of Principles" for his newspaper early in the film, and the bookend shows what becomes of it — as the case for why a mission statement is never enough.
blockquote: Eric’s earlier book, The Lean Startup, helped define a generation’s approach to entrepreneurship and innovation. Incorruptible asks what comes next: once you discover genuine value, how do you build a company capable of protecting it?

source_urls.label: Her article (Prisms of Practice, Oct 19): reads mission statements through Citizen Kane's "Declaration of Principles"
